The big idea: our six big ideas

Every programming language in the world uses these six ideas. You know them all!

Big idea It means… In Scratch
Sequence (week 1) Steps happen in order, one after another.
Loops (week 2) Repeat steps so you don’t copy them.
Events (week 3) A doorbell starts a script.
Conditionals (week 3) Ask a yes/no question, then choose.
Variables (week 4) A labeled box that remembers.
My Blocks (week 5) Name a part and use it again.

TipThe four detective steps

1. What did I expect? 2. What happened? 3. Read the blocks one at a time with your finger. 4. Change one thing, then test again.

Bug-hunt relay

Each project card shows a project that someone built with two bugs. Build it exactly as shown (bugs and all!), click the flag, then be detectives. Fill in the relay baton for each one.

New words

debugging
Finding and fixing bugs, step by step, like a detective.
Python
A programming language where you type words instead of snapping blocks.
text code
Code made of typed words and symbols.
checkpoint
A short check that shows what you know and what to practice next.
fair
Same rules for everyone, no tricks, and everyone can play.

ChallengeA bug for a friend

Build a tiny project (8 blocks or fewer) with one bug hidden inside. On a card, write what it should do, and draw or list its blocks. Bring the card to the next session: a classmate will try to find your bug!

It should:

CreativeRemix with a new theme

Make a remix of Apple Catch with a new theme, for example catching stars in space, or fish in the sea. Change the sprites, the backdrop and the sounds (from the Scratch library or drawn by you). Add a credits comment: “Remix of Apple Catch by” + your nickname, + “sprites from the Scratch library”.
